title: Test every participant and contribution record in 401(k) plan audits (Autire)
problem: Participant data (15.6 percent of sampled audits) and contributions (15.3 percent) had the highest deficiency rates in the Department of Labor's 2023 audit quality study; firms traditionally sample and test.
approach: Autire, a plan-audit platform, tests every available participant record up front and ties each flagged item to source data with dollar impact.
The vendor says tests run on hard-coded logic, so re-running on the same data gives the same result, unlike generic AI.
Vendor case studies: Belfint's average hours per audit fell from 80 to 54; Rea cut hours per audit by 40 percent (vendor-published).
The auditor decides what each flagged item means and reviewers sign off; Rea's managing director calls 100 hours to 30 overnight unrealistic.

title: AI exception analysis grouping flagged plan-audit exceptions by root cause (Autire)
problem: After testing, auditors open source files, cross-reference payroll and recordkeeper reports and decide whether each flagged item matters; on complex plans this can take several hours.
approach: Autire released Advanced AI in June 2026: it groups exceptions by failure type and shows whether an issue is isolated or systemic.
Auditors review by pattern and decide what to do with the findings and which go to the client.
The vendor says it uses Anthropic models with guardrails that filter personal data, and does not train on audit data.
Vendor-published testimonials: 50 hours per audit, about half the time before Autire, and 30 minutes to resolve flagged results; neither isolates AI.

title: Pull payroll and recordkeeper data from source systems instead of requesting files
problem: Plan-audit testing starts from sponsors' payroll registers, census files and recordkeeper reports, and Sikich names manual requests and follow-ups as something to reduce.
approach: Sikich says it has relationships with payroll and recordkeeping platforms enabling audit-request automation, and uses standardised payroll data to cut manual requests.
Vendors describe the same step: Autire lists integrations that pull payroll and recordkeeper data; AuditMiner says it standardises data across providers.
Trullion says its Data Match engine matches contribution, hire-date and vesting data across payroll registers, plan documents and custodian statements.
No outcome figures are published; an ICPAS author recommends testing the completeness and accuracy of participant data, including data a tool pulls.

title: Extract trust-statement PDFs into a trial balance and reconcile it (Autire)
problem: The trust report arrives as a PDF in each recordkeeper's own format; someone builds a trial balance from it, pulls the Form 5500, lines the two up and chases differences.
approach: Autire says an uploaded trust report is read to extract balances, contributions and distributions, checked, and turned into a trial balance.
The trial balance is shown beside other balances, with a combined view across several service providers and mid-year recordkeeper changes.
Autire's team builds each provider's format in, so the auditor does not map fields on each engagement.
The vendor says the step takes minutes instead of hours (no firm figure); a reviewing manager checks the reconciled numbers make sense.

title: Turn recordkeeper and payroll reports into standard workpapers (AuditMiner at Anders CPAs)
problem: Setting up plan-audit workpapers meant hours of manual data entry, and audits could start with incomplete client data.
approach: AuditMiner says uploading plan reports generates up to ten automated workpapers, standardised across recordkeepers, and payroll reports for testing.
Anders CPAs + Advisors automated workpaper setup and SOC report analysis with it.
Vendor-published: Anders saved hundreds of hours, for an unspecified period and engagements.
The sources do not describe machine learning or a language model, or a review step beyond staff testing instead of keying data.

title: Citation-backed assistant for plan documents, amendments and routine rule questions (Kimberlin, Sensiba)
problem: Plan documents can run past 150 pages with several amendments and detailed eligibility and compensation definitions; auditors scrolled for provisions, hand-keyed terms and asked seniors to confirm readings.
approach: Kimberlin uses CoCounsel Audit to find which plan provisions and amendments apply, including SECURE 2.0 amendments, with links to the source page.
Sensiba built CoCounsel templates for plan adoption agreements, and over 100 of its audit professionals use CoCounsel.
One Kimberlin auditor estimates a plan-document error check fell from 60-90 minutes to about 15 minutes (vendor-published).
Auditors check the cited page and section before relying on an answer.
who: Kimberlin Company, Sensiba LLP, Thomson Reuters

title: AI-assisted reading of recordkeeper and administrator SOC 1 reports for plan audits
problem: Plan audits lean on recordkeepers' and third-party administrators' SOC 1 reports, and overreliance on service providers was a deficiency theme in the Department of Labor's 2023 study.
approach: Kimberlin prompts CoCounsel Audit to map SOC 1 report controls to its testing focus areas, then copies the result into workpapers.
AuditMiner sells over 1,000 reviewed SOC toolkits turning reports into Excel workbooks and procedures; its pages describe senior-CPA review, not AI.
No outcome figure is published for SOC 1 review alone (vendor-published).
AuditMiner's toolkit terms say the auditor must review reliance decisions and conclusions; Kimberlin's case study does not describe its review step.

title: Auto-generated risk assessment from completed plan-audit planning procedures (Autire)
problem: Practitioners reported grappling with applying SAS 145, the US risk-assessment standard, to plan audits, especially identifying controls, IT systems and related parties.
approach: Autire announced in December 2024 an automated risk assessment, calculated as a by-product of the standards-based procedures performed.
It includes governance questions, a controls and walkthrough questionnaire, SOC assessments and preliminary analytics, with responses referenced to substantive procedures.
Vendor-published capability claims only; no firm results. The release does not describe how the auditor reviews or concludes on the generated assessment.

title: Plan-audit file built on a shared methodology with auto-drafted statements (DAS EBP)
problem: Caseware positions DAS EBP against outdated templates; the Department of Labor's 2023 study found deficiency rates fall as a firm's plan-audit volume rises.
approach: DAS EBP uses a plan profile to tailor the file and draft statements and disclosures from the trial balance.
Citrin Cooperman announced on 13 July 2026 that it implemented DAS including DAS EBP; the release names no plan-audit AI agent.
Caseware's releases say Withum, EisnerAmper and PKF O'Connor Davies also adopted DAS; no hours, review-note or inspection results are published (vendor-published).
Professionals complete the plan profile, run the programs and review the drafted financials.
who: Citrin Cooperman, Withum, EisnerAmper, PKF O'Connor Davies

title: Plan-specific request lists and client portals to cut what sponsors must send
problem: Plan audits run on long request lists chased by email, landing in a seasonal scramble of about four months of requests, reviews and follow-ups.
approach: Sikich uses the Suralink platform to coordinate data gathering with custom requests, progress views, per-person assignments and chat in place of email.
Autire sends plan-specific requests through a portal with reminders and status tracking.
Belfint's audit manager says audits can finish in two weeks if sponsors supply initial documents (vendor-published; a capability, not an average).
Requests can be assigned to named people, with lead time so data arrives in the correct format.

title: Firm methodology set once and enforced across plan audits (Autire)
problem: The Department of Labor found peer review does not help identify deficient plan audits: 96 of 105 deficient audits had a Pass peer review.
approach: Autire says materiality, risk logic and testing conclusions are set once at firm level and cascade to every engagement.
The vendor says its quality materials get an annual external review, and Department of Labor inspection and peer review support is included.
The vendor claims zero peer review or Department of Labor findings attributed to its platform; the claim is unverified (vendor-published).
Deviating from the configured workflow needs a deliberate override by a person; Belfint added its own extra memos.

title: Specialist plan-audit firm markets its own AI-assisted platform (Metz CPA, EBPAudit.ai)
problem: Plan audits are concentrated: in 2020, 133 firms with 100 or more plan audits did 47,982 of 86,863 audits, with far lower deficiency rates than firms with one or two.
approach: Metz CPA, which calls itself a Top 100 plan-audit firm, markets fixed three-year pricing, a written guarantee and its proprietary EBPAudit.ai platform.
It says the platform streamlines the audit and removes back-and-forth (self-reported); no turnaround figure is given.
How the AI is applied and what human checks exist are not described.

title: Form 5500 search to scope plan audits and find prospects (AuditMiner)
problem: Firms need plan information to scope a complex engagement and to find retirement plans that fit their client profile.
approach: AuditMiner's Plan Research product combines Form 5500 search with plan analytics, historical filings and audit reports.
It is used to evaluate a current engagement and to find new business.
Form 5500 is the annual return a plan files with the Department of Labor, which carries the audit report.
Product page only (vendor-published): no outcome figures, and no human checkpoint is described.

title: Idea: assess provider AI through SOC 1 reports and risk assessment
problem: Idea, not a deployment: plan data and controls sit with service providers whose AI use can change the data and controls the auditor relies on.
approach: Idea: use the AICPA's September 2026 Q&A on service-organisation AI in SOC engagements to ask providers whether AI is in the service.
Idea: use the AICPA's October 2026 practice aid on a client's AI in reporting and controls to judge SOC report coverage.
A recordkeeper's general counsel says some recordkeepers may use AI in call centres, fraud detection and monitoring; no plan-audit-specific guidance was found.
AuditMiner's toolkit terms say reliance decisions and conclusions must be reviewed by the auditor.

title: Idea: year-round plan-data monitoring shared between recordkeeper, administrator and auditor
problem: Idea, not a deployment: failed nondiscrimination tests are typically found months after the plan year closes, and plan audits cluster in a July-to-October window.
approach: Idea: reconcile contribution data monthly and track eligibility changes in real time, then extend that to a feed the auditor can use.
An audit-support firm recommends these readiness practices to sponsors; they are sponsor-side, not auditor practice.
A recordkeeper's general counsel says newer digital recordkeepers are building AI into real-time compliance monitoring, which needs clean data and ongoing integration.
No auditor has described acting on such a feed; no human checkpoint is described.
